title: Commit Coach
body:
Goal: finish a small helper that checks commit messages and warns you about secrets before you commit. (It also warms up your Level 2 skills: functions with return, lists and loops.)

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny.
  2. Finish the five TODOs:
    • is_good_message(message) returns False for messages that are empty, longer than 50 characters, boring (stuff, update, fix...) or only one word.
    • make_message("add", "star shape") returns "Add star shape".
    • find_secrets(lines) returns the lines that contain a secret word such as password or api_key (any capitals).
  3. Press Run and type some messages to try your coach. Type q to quit.

Done looks like:

Message: stuff
Be specific: say WHAT changed, like 'Add jump to hero'.
Message: Add jump to hero
Great message!

Extra: add your own boring words to BORING_MESSAGES, or make coach_tip warn when a message does not start with a capital letter.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Find the five TODO comments in starter.py. Each one is a small job. Pick the first one and read its comment slowly. The comments already tell you what to compare.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: For the checks in is_good_message, use if with return False. Use len(...) to count characters, and in to ask whether something is inside a list. For find_secrets, use a for loop on lines, with a second loop inside it.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Each check has this shape: if ____: then return False. For make_message, join the capitalized verb, a space and the thing. For find_secrets, test if ____ in ____: for each secret word, then add the line. Think about how to avoid adding one line twice.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Commit Coach - YOUR version
# A helper that checks commit messages and spots secrets before you commit.
# Finish the TODOs, then press Run and see if it does what the README says.

# Messages that do not tell future-you anything useful.
BORING_MESSAGES = ["stuff", "update", "changes", "fix", "asdf", "wip", "misc", "work"]

# Words that often mean "this line holds a secret". Secrets never go in git!
SECRET_WORDS = ["password", "passwd", "secret", "api_key", "token"]

MAX_LENGTH = 50


def is_good_message(message):
    """Return True if the commit message would help future-you."""
    text = message.strip()
    if text == "":
        return False
    # TODO 1: return False if text is longer than MAX_LENGTH
    # TODO 2: return False if text.lower() is in BORING_MESSAGES
    # TODO 3: return False if text has fewer than 2 words
    #         (hint: len(text.split()) counts the words)
    return True


def coach_tip(message):
    """Return one friendly tip about the message. (Already done!)"""
    text = message.strip()
    if text == "":
        return "Write something! Say what you changed."
    if len(text) > MAX_LENGTH:
        return f"Shorter please: {MAX_LENGTH} characters or fewer (yours has {len(text)})."
    if not is_good_message(text):
        return "Be specific: say WHAT changed, like 'Add jump to hero'."
    return "Great message!"


def make_message(verb, thing):
    """Build a message like 'Add star shape' from a verb and a thing."""
    # TODO 4: return the verb with a capital first letter, a space, then the thing.
    #         hint: "add".capitalize() gives "Add"
    return ""


def find_secrets(lines):
    """Return a list of the lines that look like they hold a secret."""
    found = []
    # TODO 5: loop over every line. If any word from SECRET_WORDS is inside
    #         line.lower(), append the line to found (only once per line).
    return found


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Commit Coach: type a commit message and get a tip.")
    print("Type q to quit.")
    while True:
        message = input("Message: ")
        if message.strip().lower() == "q":
            print("Happy committing!")
            break
        print(coach_tip(message))
